answer: Two ways to guard a gate. One checks papers once and trusts them forever. A farm prints a thousand papers. The other asks for a live signal. On a mesa at dawn, a sparrow tells you which birds are real, because strangers hear every song and gain nothing from lying. An agent proves itself the same way, confirmed by clients it never met. Bribing every witness costs more than the job pays. A newcomer waits to be heard, and that wait is the price of the gate.
